<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **82** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `025070464d143a890f661ec7b2fb34129adc2802` — the merge of head `7b8cb65be011a7b203c8440f157bd79158b1529f` into base `a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 025070464d143a890f661ec7b2fb34129adc2802 && git checkout 025070464d143a890f661ec7b2fb34129adc2802
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f 7b8cb65be011a7b203c8440f157bd79158b1529f && git checkout -B drift-repro a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f && git merge --no-ff 7b8cb65be011a7b203c8440f157bd79158b1529f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a57a007d81c819fc2fdf15e9c240e9f5e273b13f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31872 (S2 #31683) at head b5471c22: CHANGES, one required fix (R3 only).**

**What passes**
- The columns use D8's own names. They are nullable, users cannot write them, and no reader or writer moves onto them, which keeps red line 3. The CONTROL shows `/auth/me/permissions` byte-identical whether the column is null, filled or forged.
- No unique key changes, so S1's package-less bar does not come up.
- The backfill waits for the holder seal, asks the one D3 rule (core `resolvePackageScopedHolders` / objectql `resolvePackageScopedName`), and never takes the first holder.
- A refusal stays null and names every candidate, so red line 2 holds. A second run writes 0 rows.
- R1, R5, R6 and R13 asked with no caller package are right:
  - An R1 grant is the environment's.
  - The R5, R6 and R13 columns record which item the row is *of* (the rule, the queue, the rule's cursor), and none of those rows names an authoring package.
- The duplicated walker, the census recount from 276 to 278, and the zh labels are fine.

**R1 (required): an R3 suggestion is a package's own reference, so it is resolved from that package.**

A `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` row has `package_id`, the package that made the suggestion. ADR-0150 D3 says a reference resolves from the package that wrote it, as `position.permissionSets` does from the declaring package (D7). Asking with no caller package can bind a package's reference to a holder outside its closure.

The case: P suggests `s` and only an unrelated U holds `s`. This head writes `permission_set_package = U` and then reports that it "differs". The column is the stored answer that the permission-set B child will trust, so a stored loosening would sit in the table waiting for its reader. Red line 1 forbids that, and a report does not undo a write.

Fix:
- For R3, pass `callerPackageId` = the row's `package_id`, or null when the row has none.
- A refusal for that caller (`outside-closure`, `ambiguous-in-closure`) stays null and is reported with its candidates, like any refusal.
- The step-1 own holding binds P even beside a pre-phase-1 clash with U. That is D3's target answer, and the changeset should say so.
- "Differs" then means only "held by a declared dependency of the suggesting package". Keep reporting it.

Pins:
- A suggestion from P where only an unrelated U holds the set stays null and is reported. Run it with the fix ablated (red), then with it (green).
- P→D, where D holds the set: bound to D and reported as differing.
- P beside a U clash: bound to P.

R1, R5, R6 and R13 are unchanged.

Re-ping the epic seat with the new head.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31872 (S2 #31683) at head 7b8cb65b: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

**My R1 from 6735731423 is met.**
- R3 is asked with `callerPackageId` = the row's `package_id` (null when the row has none). The resolution goes through the same core `resolvePackageScopedHolders` and the same `packageScopedHoldersOf` slice, so there is still one rule.
- The update is per row, by `id`, using that row's own caller. Rows that share a name but come from different packages are never bound together.
- A refusal for the caller stays null and is reported with its reason, the writing package and every candidate.
- Step 1 (P beside a clash with U) binds P, and the changeset states that as D3's answer.
- "Differs" now means only a declared dependency of the suggesting package.
- The pins cover U-only (null, outside-closure), P→D (D, reported as differing), P+U (P), and D+D2 (null, ambiguous-in-closure). Dropping the caller column turns 5 of them red; take-first turns 8 red.
- R1, R5, R6 and R13 are unchanged and asked with no caller package.

**Red lines 1–3 hold.** Every stored answer is the writing package's own D3 answer or null, the backfill never takes the first holder, and no reader moves.

**Owed to later children:**
- The permission-set B child and S4 read these columns. Each one's writer starts stamping in the same PR as its reader, so rows written after boot stop waiting for the next boot pass.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31872 (Fixes #31683, ADR-0150 child S2) · 2026-11-09T09:16Z

Head-sha: `7b8cb65b`

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The whole card lands here under `Fixes #31683`. `Clause-②: no`: the columns are stored only, and no reader, route or authored shape changes. `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Seat ruling 6734560017, as narrowed by the epic for R3:** the columns use D8's names. R1 and R3 get `permission_set_package`, managed R5 rows get `package_id` (admin rows stay null), R6 gets `queue_package`, and R13 gets `rule_package`. Each is nullable and read-only. No unique key changes: every index is pinned byte-identical, and the store refuses a duplicate on each key whatever the package column holds. Writers do not stamp yet; the body names the hand-off to each reader child.
- **Backfill:** it runs at `kernel:bootstrapped` after `bareNameHoldersAreSealed`, walks only rows whose column is null, and asks the one D3 rule (core `resolvePackageScopedHolders` in plugin-security, objectql `resolvePackageScopedName` in plugin-sharing). R1, R5, R6 and R13 ask with no caller package, because each column identifies the row's own item or an environment grant. R3 asks from the suggesting package (`callerPackageId` = the row's `package_id`), per the epic's CHANGES. A unique holder binds. A refusal, environment or platform holder, or no holder stays null and is reported, a refusal naming every candidate. A second run writes 0 rows with the same report. The suggesting package's own set binds beside a pre-phase-1 clash (step 1), as the changeset says.
- **Pins and ablations:** plugin tests on real ObjectQL and SqlDriver. R3: U-only stays null, P depending on D binds D and is reported as differing, P beside a U clash binds P, and a D+D2 clash in the closure stays null naming both. Dogfood 7/7 across restarts. CONTROL: `/auth/me/permissions` is byte-identical with the column null, filled and forged. 11 ablations across the two rounds (take-first, caller dropped, second run, R5 filter, seal wait, R3 differs, widened key) are each red, then restored.
- **Epic review:** CHANGES at `b5471c22` (R3 only), then PASS at `7b8cb65b`. The duplicated row walker (paging and writing only, so no package root gains an export) is ruled not a second mechanism. ADR-0150 readings (a)–(d) are in the body.
- **Declared deviations:** the tenant-audit census is recounted to 279 for the two new backfill write sites, and zh-CN and zh-Hant labels are translated because a queue test requires them.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --pr 31872`: NOT governed, 2000 changed lines. K = 3 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 103/103 exit 0, `--ran` reconciled. plugin-security 6068 and plugin-sharing 1504 pass; lint and typecheck exit 0. CI on this head is running; auto-merge waits for it.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31683, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closed by `Fixes`.
